$comment: The documented distribution scope for native packages (D34).

This file is what makes a platform 'required'. The release check derives its requirements from the lockfile intersected with the platforms listed here, so nobody can quietly drop a platform by editing a review record: dropping one means editing this file, which names a decision, an approver and a date.

An exclusion is not 'we did not get to it'. It is a recorded decision that the project does not distribute for that platform, with a reason. An excluded platform still appears in observations if npm locks it; it simply does not block a release.

A packagePattern exclusion matches by name on every platform at once, so it may name only packages that no platform listed below requires; scripts/native-reconcile.mjs refuses one that matches a required package, whatever decision it cites (D177). A platform leaves scope through an os/cpu exclusion. sharp and @img/sharp-wasm32, which npm installs on every platform, stay required whatever this file lists.
Node.js 22.x on Mac, Windows and Linux is the supported runtime (ERD section 08 TOOL, install guide section 1). The platform list below follows from that.
